title: Problem Setup: Decomposing the Nonderogatory Cyclic Vector Theorem
content: The module decomposes the proof into three pieces: (1) PROVED: e₀ is cyclic for companion matrices via the Krylov orbit, (2) AXIOM: nonderogatory matrices are similar to their companion matrices, (3) PROVED: cyclic vectors transfer under similarity. Definitions: IsCyclicVector says no nonzero polynomial of degree < n annihilates v under M; IsNonderogatory says minpoly = charpoly.
mathContext: A vector $v$ is cyclic for $M \in M_n(K)$ iff $\{v, Mv, \ldots, M^{n-1}v\}$ spans $K^n$. A matrix is nonderogatory iff $\text{minpoly}(M) = \text{charpoly}(M)$, i.e., it has a single invariant factor.

title: Companion Matrix and Krylov Orbit: C^k e₀ = e_k
content: Defines companionMat(p) with 1s on the subdiagonal, negated coefficients in the last column, and 0s elsewhere. Three structural lemmas characterize entries. The key orbit lemma companionMat_pow_e0 (line 96) proves C^k e₀ = e_k for k < n by induction: the subdiagonal shift C·e_j = e_{j+1} is the single step, composed k times.
mathContext: The companion matrix $C(p)$ of monic degree-$n$ polynomial $p$ satisfies $C^k e_0 = e_k$ for $k < n$. This means the Krylov subspace $\text{span}\{e_0, Ce_0, \ldots, C^{n-1}e_0\} = K^n$.

title: Leading Coefficient Extraction via Orbit Evaluation
content: companion_orbit_eval (line 122): for nonzero q with deg(q) < n, evaluating (q(C)·e₀) at coordinate natDegree(q) gives q.leadingCoeff. Expands aeval as a sum over support, distributes mulVec (via sum_mulVec), substitutes C^k e₀ = e_k, then collapses to the single surviving term at k = natDegree(q) using Finset.sum_eq_single. This extraction trick avoids dimension/rank arguments.
mathContext: Key identity: $(q(C) \cdot e_0)_{\deg(q)} = \text{lc}(q)$. Since $C^k e_0 = e_k$, we get $(q(C)e_0)_j = q_j$ for $j \leq \deg(q)$. At $j = \deg(q)$, this is the leading coefficient.

title: Main Verified Result: e₀ is Cyclic for Companion Matrices
content: companionMat_e0_cyclic (line 169): for any monic polynomial p of degree n > 0, e₀ is cyclic for C(p). Proof by contrapositive: if q ≠ 0 with deg(q) < n and q(C)e₀ = 0, then evaluating at coordinate natDegree(q) gives q.leadingCoeff = 0, contradicting q ≠ 0. This elegantly avoids linear independence or dimension arguments.
mathContext: If $q(C(p))e_0 = 0$ and $\deg(q) < n$, then $(q(C)e_0)_{\deg(q)} = 0$. But $(q(C)e_0)_{\deg(q)} = \text{lc}(q) \neq 0$ for $q \neq 0$. Contradiction.

title: Similarity Transfer and the Nonderogatory Axiom
content:
cyclic_vector_similar_transfer (line 188): if M = P⁻¹NP and v is cyclic for N, then P⁻¹v is cyclic for M. Uses the conjugation formula q(P⁻¹NP) = P⁻¹q(N)P, proved by induction on monomials.

nonderogatory_similar_to_companion (line 242): the axiom that nonderogatory M is similar to C(charpoly(M)). This is the classical single-invariant-factor theorem requiring rational canonical form (PID structure theorem), absent from Mathlib. Precisely stated rather than left as a vague sorry.
mathContext: Conjugation: $q(P^{-1}NP) = P^{-1}q(N)P$. The axiom: $\text{minpoly}(M) = \text{charpoly}(M) \Rightarrow \exists P: M = P^{-1}C(\chi_M)P$.

title: Main Theorem: Nonderogatory Matrices Have Cyclic Vectors (Any Field)
content: nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_any_field (line 266): combines e₀ cyclic for C(charpoly M) (proved), M similar to C(charpoly M) (axiom), and similarity transfers cyclic vectors (proved). The n=0 case is trivial. Corollary nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_finite (line 283) specializes to finite fields, removing the [Infinite K] hypothesis. The companion matrix approach is purely algebraic — no cardinality/density assumptions needed.
mathContext: For $n > 0$: $e_0$ is cyclic for $C(\chi_M)$ (orbit argument); $M \sim C(\chi_M)$ (axiom); $P^{-1}e_0$ is cyclic for $M$ (transfer). Works over any field $K$.
